input.quote: In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.1 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: Article 14.2 imposes fixed, formula-driven termination payments on PB (our party): 300% of Development Costs where SFJ terminates for PB's material breach (14.2.1), on PB's at-will termination (14.2.2), on SFJ's bankruptcy termination (14.2.5.2) and on safety terminations attributable to PB (14.2.7); 150% on a Change of Control termination (14.2.6) and a compliance breach (14.2.8.1); 100% on Adverse Patent Impact (14.2.9); and Development Costs plus 25% annual interest on a JSC-decision termination (14.2.10). These are liquidated amounts payable by Customer, and the breach-triggered multiples sit in walk-away territory because they are punitive multiples of SFJ's spend and, under 14.2.1, are expressly cumulative with SFJ's right "to pursue remedies it may have at law or equity for such breach, including the right to seek damages." That fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees). We have taken the fallback rather than preferred because an unconditional prohibition would require conforming eight separate retained payment formulas; instead one governing subsection caps PB's liquidated exposure at a sole early-termination fee of three months of Development Costs (the recurring funding metric that is the base of every existing formula). The late-payment interest in Section 6.4 is ordinary default interest, not a liquidated amount, and is not flagged.

proposal.summary: Cap PB's liquidated exposure on any termination at a single early-termination fee of three months of Development Costs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 300%/150% termination multiples are liquidated amounts payable by us, so we have added a single governing cap: the only liquidated amount payable by PB on any termination is an early-termination fee of no more than three months of Development Costs. Our preferred position is no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties at all; this three-month cap is our fallback.

ops.text: Liquidated Amounts. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 14.2, the sole liquidated amount payable by PB in connection with any termination of this Agreement is an early-termination fee not exceeding three months of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ.

mappings.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
